To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) amino substitution at the 5-position affects the ultrafast deactivation of 5-substituted uracls; 2) amino substitution at 6-position does not affect the ultrafast deacation of 6-substituted uracls; 3) amino substitution affects the out-of-plane motions in the S1 state of 5-substutited uracls.

the amino group of 5AU affects the out-of-plane motions of the 5-CH3 group and the excited state relaxation of the molecule, leading to a slower fluorescence decay, while the amino group of the 6AU has a negligible effect on the excited state relaxation.

the excited state dynamics and relaxation of 6-aminopurine is similar to uracil, whereas the relaxation of 5-aminopurin is fundamentally different, and involves the formation of a new transient excited state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of excited state deactivation in uracil derivatives in aqueous solution by means of femtosecond spectroscopy.
the excited state relaxation processes of amino substituted uracils, and in particular, the role that the amino group plays in the excited state dynamics.
the effect of amino substitution on excited state dynamics of the nucleic acid bases uracil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
amino groups in general, and the 6-amino group in particular, do not affect the excited state deactivation dynamics of uracils.
amino substitution affects the ultrafast relaxation dynamics of the uracil chromophore by modifying the out-of-plane motions of the 5- or 6-substituents.

the amino group in 6AU does not affect the ultrafast relaxation of the uracil chromophore, while in 5AU the amino group affects both the ultrafast and the slow relaxation processes of the chromophore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amino substitution in the 5 position of uracil affects the out-of-plane dynamics of the molecule, while the amino group in the 6 position has no influence on the ultrafast dynamics of the molecule.
the amino group, which is known to be an efficient quencher for the excited states of many molecules, is not effective in quenching the fluorescence of uracil derivatives.
amino-substituted pyrimidines have a very complex photophysics, which cannot be described in the simple terms of excited state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT).

amino substitution can have a dramatic effect on the dynamics of the excited states of the nucleobase.
the presence of an amino group in the 5-position affects the dynamics of uracils in a way that cannot be predicted from previous observations in uracils lacking this substitution.
